about:
Six resilient materials with the dynamic modulus of elasticity a floating floor is designed with, from Table 8.3, "Dynamic modulus of elasticity". The page prints the density in kg/m3 and the modulus in MPa, and every modulus and all but one density as a range; the modulus is held in pascals. The glass wool density is printed "approx. 125" and held as approximate. The two rock wool rows share a name and are told apart only by their densities, which is why their keys carry them.

The modulus heading carries the load it was measured under, "(static load ≈ 2 kPa)", which is on every row as static_load_pa and marked approximate. The running text above the table says the same and adds how much that matters: rock wool of 150 to 175 kg/m3 is about 0.3 MPa at 2 kPa, about 20 per cent lower at 1 kPa and about 30 per cent higher at 4 kPa. A dynamic modulus is a property of the layer under its load and not of the material alone.

These are moduli and not dynamic stiffnesses: the stiffness per unit area of a layer is its modulus divided by its thickness, s' = E_dyn / d, and the page prints no thickness. The table credits no source.
